title: Lift Equation
learningObjectives: Explain how lift varies with air density, the square of velocity, wing area, body shape and inclination.
Use the lift coefficient Cl to collect complex dependencies into a single variable for calculation.
Apply L = Cl·(rho·V²/2)·A and describe dynamic pressure as (rho·V²/2).

explanations.text: Lift is influenced by air density, the square of velocity, surface area, body shape, inclination to the flow, viscosity and compressibility.

evidence.quote: Lift depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air's viscosity and compressibility

explanations.text: Complex shape and flow effects can be collected into a single lift coefficient Cl, giving the lift equation where lift equals Cl times density times half velocity squared times wing area.

evidence.quote: For lift, this variable is called the lift coefficient, designated "Cl."
The lift equation states that lift L is equal to the lift coefficient Cl times the density rho times half of the velocity V squared times the wing area A.

explanations.text: In the equation rho denotes air density, and the term density times velocity squared over two is called dynamic pressure.

evidence.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho.
The combination of terms "density times the square of the velocity divided by two" is called the dynamic pressure
